Amanda — thanks for the clear list. Quick overview below; I attached a short term/price summary and a sample pricing sheet for reference. Happy to review live if you prefer.

High-level commercial constructs we commonly propose (pilot -> production):

1) Anchored platform fee (annualized) + operator licenses
   - Platform fee: a single annual platform fee that covers the private control plane, orchestration, and core observability. We can amortize this across Year 1 (recommended for pilots converting to full prod).
   - Operator licenses: per-site operator license (recommended for multi-site deployments) or a per-node alternative for high-density clusters.

2) Metered consumption + reduced platform fee
   - Lower up-front platform fee with metered tokens/throughput for teams that prefer OPEX. Good for unpredictable workloads; we provide burst caps.

3) Hybrid (anchors + consumption buffer)
   - Anchor a smaller platform fee with a usage floor and node-based overage that kicks in once pilot thresholds are passed.

Pilot incentives / amortization playbook:
- Typical pilot credit: 20–40% off platform fee for 3 months; if Crestline converts to annual commitment within 90 days, we amortize the pilot credit over the first 12 months (reduces invoices, not list price).
- Implementation credits: limited SOW hours can be included as a one-time onboarding credit.

Support tiers & SRE retainer:
- Standard: business hours (M–F 8x5), 4 business-hour response for P1, 1 business-day for P2.
- Priority: 24x7 monitoring + 1-hour P1 response, 4-hour P2 response.
- SRE Retainer: block of hours (e.g., 100/200 hours) for runbook creation, on-call overlap during cutovers, and incident remediation with guaranteed SLO escalation paths. Retainer rate is discounted against ad hoc time-and-materials.
- Credits: we include incident credits tied to availability SLAs in Enterprise contracts.

- Marissa will slot a tailored quote and a DocuSign-ready PDF; we can provide a 30-min call on Monday 9/21 if that helps for procurement readout prep.

Amanda — looping in some technical notes that often influence commercial decisions (I’ll keep this high level):

1) SRE retainer usage: typically used for runbook authoring, playbook rehearsals during cutover, and major incident handoffs. For a 3-site pilot we see most customers purchase a 100-hour block; for full production we recommend 200–400 hours depending on daily change velocity.

2) Observability addon: includes extended metrics retention + alerting runbooks. Pricing: $8k/mo baseline for up to 30 days retention; longer retention tiers priced separately. This reduces time-to-detect and materially lowers P1 MTTR in our historical data (useful when evaluating SLA credits).

3) Operator license vs node model: operator-per-site simplifies legal & invoicing for multi-site customers. Node-based is more granular for high-density single-site clusters. If Crestline expects bursts or increases in GPU count, we should model both: a per-site anchor + optional node add-on makes the quote predictable but flexible.

4) Implementation risk & SOW: the SOW should include a short forgiveness window for early integration items (we typically include a 15–20 hour buffer in the first month). That buffer can be drawn from the implementation credit line in the commercial offer.

I’ve included the prior messages below for continuity. If Crestline wants a technical breakout for procurement (networking requirements, KMS/HSM options, observability endpoints), we can provide a 1–2 page tech appendix to attach to the quote.
